thread:
Amy S.: heads up — procurement flagged a mismatch on the marketplace invoice for the ACME POC. they say the rate is different than the committed rate in the SOW. can someone help? :thinking:
Raj P.: which invoice/line? marketplace invoices are messy (publishers + marketplace fee). do you have the PDF?
Amy S.: attached the screenshot in email. quick excerpt: `LineItem: Redwood Inference — Usage (Committed) 1000 units @ $0.015` but PO says $0.012. procurement put a hold.
Leah F.: ok. likely the marketplace grossed up fees or we routed through a different sku. is this a committed seat or marketplace consumed seats?
Amy S.: this customer committed to a monthly commit via marketplace private offer. they gave a PO to their procurement team referencing the commit rate.
Raj P.: if it's a Marketplace Private Offer, billing entity might differ. AWS/Azure add platform fees which can show separately. we need to confirm the invoice entity and the applied rate.
Mike R.: looping finance. @Leah F. can you check deal desk record for that PO id and confirm that a marketplace private offer with a discount was sent?
Leah F.: checking... deal desk record shows a 20% off list on the publisher-side commit, approval stamped. the private offer id is PO-ACME-472. marketplace fee should not alter the publisher unit price in the line item but sometimes the UI aggregates.
Julia K.: from security/legal — procurement is asking for net-30 payment terms and a copy of our marketplace contract. marketplace sales flow often enforces platform terms. do we have a way to surface the private offer terms to customers?
Amy S.: procurement won't lift hold until invoice aligns to PO. they want the exact line rate.
Raj P.: short fix: can we issue a credit memo to reflect the committed rate and apply it to the invoice? finance may prefer adjusting the next invoice rather than reissuing.
Leah F.: finance prefers a credit when platform already issued. @Mike R., approve if credit memo for difference is ok.
Mike R.: ok from revops side to do a credit memo for the delta once finance confirms. but we need internal signoff for a special term: this commit had an approved 20% off, which is >15% threshold — deal desk notes say finance + legal must sign off on credits for >15% discounts.
Raj P.: thanks. @Leah F. can you attach the deal desk approval thread? procurement wants a paper trail too.
Leah F.: attaching the approval PDF link: https://redwood.s3/approvals/PO-ACME-472.pdf
billing-bot: invoice 2026-03-07-ACME created by marketplace-bridge. Line breakdown: publisher_charge $12,000; platform_fee $720; tax $240; total $12,960.
Amy S.: procurement: "we need the invoice to reflect the committed unit price and the PO number on each line." they won't accept a platform-level fee line item without explanation.
Julia K.: we should send them a one-page explanation: 1) committed unit price (publisher-side) 2) marketplace/platform fee separate 3) proof of private offer acceptance. I can draft a note and legal can stamp it.
Raj P.: also note that marketplace payouts can lag and ultimately billing is handled by the marketplace, not Redwood. that often confuses procurement. include a note about billing entity and tax id.
Leah F.: action items: (1) finance to confirm if credit memo or invoice reissue (2) legal to generate a one-pager explaining marketplace mechanics + private offer reference (3) sales to coordinate PO entity mapping with customer procurement.
Amy S.: timeline: procurement expects an answer by EOD tomorrow or they will escalate to their vendor management group.
Mike R.: I'll queue a fast-path review with finance. @Leah F. please flag this as high priority on the deal desk queue.
Leah F.: flagged. also confirming: since this is a committed monthly seat commit, we need to ensure future invoices reflect the correct SKU mapping — I will update the billing mapping doc and drop the snippet here.
Raj P.: quick FYI for next steps on POC coordination — if they are doing a usage reconciliation POC, recommend we capture a short sample report showing tokens/embeddings usage vs commit so procurement sees the consumption math.
Amy S.: perfect. any blockers on special terms approval?
Leah F.: legal needs to review the contract amendment for net-30 + the >15% discount memo. I put a note in Legal queue.
Julia K.: I'll take the one-pager and the contract amendment review.
Amy S.: thanks all — I'll update the customer and push for the PO mapping. :thumbsup:
Mike R.: note for the record: until the credit/invoice is done, procurement hold remains. expect ~48-72h to clear after finance action.
Amy S.: great. will keep thread updated with evidence for procurement.
Raj P.: if anything stalls, escalate to me and I'll call their procurement lead.
Amy S.: thanks — closing loop after finance confirms.
